world.setting: A present-day deep dive into David Brooks's argument: two life-mountains with a valley of collapse between them, drawn as slopes, kitchens, hospitals and streets; Tolstoy's Russia, Wordsworth's England and Lincoln's Washington appear only as stories.

brooks.name: David Brooks
brooks.look: A fifty-something American writer with thinning grey-brown hair, rimless glasses, rumpled navy blazer over an open-collar blue shirt, a slightly stooped, thoughtful posture.

everyman.name: Everyman
everyman.look: A thirty-something office worker with dark hair in a ponytail, grey hoodie, lanyard around the neck, tired eyes - the listener climbing the first mountain.

tolstoy.name: Leo Tolstoy
tolstoy.look: Leo Tolstoy: an elderly Russian novelist with a long white beard, brown peasant tunic with a rope belt, deep-set sorrowful eyes.

wordsworth.name: William Wordsworth
wordsworth.look: A young William Wordsworth in the 1790s: lanky, dark hair to the collar, olive greatcoat and cream cravat, gazing at the dawn.

kathy.name: Kathy Fletcher
kathy.look: Kathy Fletcher: a warm middle-aged Washington mother with a short silver-blonde bob, red cardigan and an apron, a ladle in hand.

david-simpson.name: David Simpson
david-simpson.look: David Simpson: a broad, gentle middle-aged man with a grey beard, green flannel shirt, sleeves rolled, sitting at a crowded dinner table.

lincoln.name: Abraham Lincoln
lincoln.look: Abraham Lincoln: very tall and gaunt, black frock coat, black bowtie, dark hair and chin beard, a stovepipe hat.

mcclellan.name: General McClellan
mcclellan.look: General George McClellan: a short, proud Union general in a dark blue uniform with brass buttons and a kepi, moustache, chin held high.

luke.name: Luke
luke.look: Luke, a hospital janitor: a quiet man in his forties with a shaved head, pale teal work uniform, a cleaning cart beside him.

kitchen.look: A family kitchen late on a rainy Tuesday night - where the vow is tested.

hospital.look: A hospital corridor and room at night - where Luke works and families grieve.

room.look: A quiet apartment room with a single lamp - Brooks alone after the divorce.

street.look: A Washington D.C. street at dusk with row houses.

office.look: A glass office with a calendar full of obligations - the first mountain at work.

horizon.look: A wide open horizon with distant ridgelines - the mountains of the book.

library.look: A study with old books and handwriting on a desk - for Wordsworth and the poets.

objects.why: Each mountain's top - the first is achievement, the second is commitment
The first-mountain climb of status and resume
The heart and soul exposed in the valley; moral sentimentalism
The commitment to a spouse and family; the vow
The prize of the first mountain that turns out hollow
The polished ego ideal presented to the world
The first-mountain skill hung on the wall, then used to defend someone
Opening the front door to the neighborhood
The call: what is life asking of me?

spine.claim: Self-fulfillment is the wrong project: the first mountain's summit leaves you alone and hollow, as Brooks's own collapse after 2013 shows.
The valley between the mountains - winning and finding it empty, or being knocked off - breaks the ego ideal open and exposes the big shaggy.
The second mountain starts with a call: vocation, then vows to a spouse and family that outlast the feeling.
Community and faith turn the I into a we - thick connections, planted lives, strength not self-generated - and the framework survives its author's privilege.
The first mountain's skills are reoriented, not wasted; the question changes from what can I achieve to what have I already promised?

signatureObjects.name: The Two Mountains
signatureObjects.why: The book's central picture: a lower peak on the left (achievement, ego), a deep valley between, a higher peak on the right (commitment, the 'we') - no shared icon draws a pair of peaks with a valley.

signatureObjects.name: Crooked Timber
signatureObjects.why: Kant's metaphor for marriage: warped planks lashed together so they hold up a roof.

signatureObjects.name: The Treadmill
signatureObjects.why: Narrator image for the first mountain: a treadmill disguised as a staircase - effort without arrival

signatureObjects.name: The Wedding Rings
signatureObjects.why: The vow: a promise made before the feeling, the moral scaffolding of marriage

signatureObjects.name: The Crowded Dinner Table
signatureObjects.why: Kathy and David feeding 26 kids every Thursday - thick connection

signatureObjects.name: The Sword on the Wall
signatureObjects.why: The first-mountain skill hung as a status symbol, then taken down to defend someone

signatureObjects.name: The Big Shaggy
signatureObjects.why: Annie Dillard/Brooks image for the wild untamed unconscious region of the heart and soul that suffering exposes

signatureObjects.name: The Drained Battery
signatureObjects.why: Giving and community drain you: burnout, depleted willpower, the limits of personal steam
